The 0.5 PPR scoring system introduces a probabilistic element where TE value is derived from projected FPTS, which are aggregated from multiple free sources including FantasyPros and FanDuel Research. The model’s failure mode arises from reliance on outdated or inconsistent projections, particularly when players are sidelined (e.g., Bowers) or face high-risk matchups (e.g., Kraft post-ACL). DST selection hinges on opponent rank, but lacks salary data, leading to potential misalignment between value and cost. The dual nature of the model—player and defense—is susceptible to overfitting if projections are not robustly validated across sources. Temporal logic ensures that eligibility rules are applied consistently across game slates, while Bayesian inference allows for uncertainty quantification in projected outcomes.
